newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan seen buying 60-70,000 tonnes Canadian canola.
newsitem.headline: Japan seen buying 60-70,000 tonnes Canadian canola.

text.p: Japan will buy 60,000 to 70,000 tonnes of Canadian canola by the end of December for January shipment, local traders said on Thursday.
The Winnipeg Commodity Exchange's nearby canola prices ended up on Wednesday on rumours of large Japanese demand.
"Yes, we returned to the market this week," a grain trader at a major trade house said.
"Bullish sentiment is emerging in canola markets and it's better to cover Canadian canola for January shipment now," the trader said.
Local traders are currently buying Canadian canola for January to March shipment.
"Considering the price gap with U.S. soybeans, Canadian canola prices are at a reasonable level at the moment," another grain trader in Tokyo said.
